reference.source: Journal of Inherited Metabolic Disease / textbooks of clinical immunology and metabolism
clinicalPearls: A rare disorder defined by persistent, marked elevation of serum zinc together with grossly raised circulating calprotectin (the S100A8/S100A9 complex)
Patients typically have chronic systemic inflammation with recurrent fever, anaemia of chronic disease, hepatosplenomegaly, and failure to thrive
It sits on a spectrum with the autoinflammatory condition often described alongside recurrent infections and arthritis
The extreme hyperzincaemia is artefactual in the sense that most zinc is bound to the vast excess of circulating calprotectin, so tissues may paradoxically be functionally zinc-deficient
Very high serum zinc with disproportionate inflammation should prompt measurement of calprotectin
Anaemia is common and may be refractory, reflecting chronic inflammation and disturbed metal handling
Distinguishing it from primary immunodeficiency and other autoinflammatory syndromes requires careful phenotyping
Management is supportive and anti-inflammatory, treating flares and complications rather than the zinc level itself
reference.pathophysiology: Hyperzincaemia with hypercalprotectinaemia is characterised by massive overproduction or release of calprotectin, a zinc- and calcium-binding heterocomplex of the S100A8 and S100A9 proteins that is abundant in neutrophils and monocytes and is a key mediator of innate immune inflammation. The enormous circulating pool of calprotectin sequesters zinc, elevating measured serum zinc to striking levels while reducing zinc availability to tissues. Sustained calprotectin-driven inflammation produces the systemic features: fever, anaemia of chronic disease, organomegaly, and growth failure. The disorder illustrates how an inflammatory metal-binding protein can distort trace-element measurements and drive a chronic inflammatory phenotype.
additionalDifferentials: Systemic-onset juvenile idiopathic arthritis and other autoinflammatory syndromes
Malignancy causing chronic inflammation and anaemia
Other causes of anaemia of chronic disease with organomegaly
additionalInvestigations: Inflammatory markers including C-reactive protein and ferritin
Full blood count and iron studies for anaemia of chronic disease
Immunological and autoinflammatory workup to exclude alternatives
redFlags: Persistent high fever with organomegaly suggesting a severe inflammatory flare
Features of macrophage activation or systemic decompensation
Failure to thrive with growth arrest in a child
reference.prognosis: A chronic relapsing inflammatory disorder; severity varies, with anaemia, growth failure, and recurrent inflammation causing morbidity, while the biochemical hyperzincaemia itself does not require correction.
pitfalls: Misinterpreting the very high serum zinc as clinically meaningful zinc excess or attempting to lower it
Overlooking functional tissue zinc deficiency despite high serum levels
Failing to measure calprotectin when confronted with unexplained hyperzincaemia and inflammation
Confusing the picture with a primary immunodeficiency or malignancy without full phenotyping
references: Textbooks of clinical immunology and metabolic medicine
management: Direct treatment at suppressing the calprotectin-driven inflammation with anti-inflammatory agents such as corticosteroids, trialling biologic therapy (for example interleukin-1 or interleukin-6 blockade) in refractory autoinflammation
Do not attempt to lower the serum zinc, since the hyperzincaemia is an artefact of calprotectin binding and needs no correction
Manage anaemia of chronic disease supportively, treating coexisting iron deficiency and reserving transfusion for symptomatic anaemia
Monitor inflammatory markers such as C-reactive protein and ferritin, alongside circulating calprotectin, to gauge disease activity and treatment response
Surveil growth, nutrition and organomegaly, with paediatric input for failure to thrive
Refer to metabolic medicine and clinical immunology or rheumatology for co-ordinated autoinflammatory care
Escalate immunomodulation during severe inflammatory flares with fever and worsening anaemia
